title: INC. Plant Protein 1kg $26.99 / 2kg $44.99 + Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store) @ Chemist Warehouse
body:
Deal: INC. Plant Protein 1kg $26.99 / 2kg $44.99 + Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store) @ Chemist Warehouse

[Kemikemi] Thank you. WPI hiked up crazy so this is my alternative solution as being a lactose intolerant
[biznis] how is this compared to the coles wellness road pea protien?
[BestTechAdvisor] The Coles product is 100% pea protein. INC.'s powder contains a blend for a better balance of amino acids. It's also flavoured and ready to drink with water/milk, whereas the 100% pea protein would need to be added to something like a banana smoothie to be palatable.
[Wip3out] Very hard to compare as I feel like they're basically different products. Be like comparing plain milk to choc milk.
I always have both in the pantry, unflavoured pea for adding to meals, the INC plant choc and vanilla for shakes.
[pr0o] Hey guys
First time in life, thinking about buying protein powder
Dont care whether veg or not. Please suggest best protein for muscles, value to moneu
[earth2vincent] this one is easily one of the best value protein powders. most people prefer whey protein isolate (wpi) but the price is insane rn. i've swapped to plant-based ones like this and they do the same job.
all you need to really worry about is if the powder is a complete protein (covers all essential amino acids) which it does.
[pr0o] But only 49% protein.. how is this good value? Shouldnt there be 80% protein at least?
I'm thinking this
https://www.chemistwarehouse.com.au/buy/109077/inc-100-dynam…
[BestTechAdvisor] How'd you arrive at 49%? It's >70% protein.
[BestTechAdvisor] Purely through the lens of muscle growth, whey is better than plant protein. Isolate (WPI) is better than standard whey (WPC) but is much more expensive and you won't get much benefit if you're not a performance athlete.
The gap between quality plant protein blends and whey also isn't worth worrying about… unless you're a pro athlete. People who choose plant proteins over whey tend to do so because of lactose intolerance or ethics. There are many different types of plant proteins so if one doesn't agree with you, don't let that stop you from trying another.
A lot of brands also of cheap sample satchels.
[earth2vincent] has anyone tried the vanilla flavour? is it any good? ive tried the chocolate and berry one. berry flavour is delicious and chocolate is meh.
[DraggyX] Do they have grainy/chalky taste like other plant bae protein?
[earth2vincent] i dont really properly mix mine bc im a lazy (profanity) so yeah its a bit powdery but i'm sure if you use a shaker bottle it'd be fine.
the berry flavour is actually quite pleasant and i keep like 5x2kg tubs because i like it so much.
[Wip3out] Not as chalky as others I'd tried (Musashi for example sucks for chalkiness, so does Bondi Protein), if having the 1 scoop with 300ml its barely noticeable to me, but depends how sensitive you are. I often have 1.5 or 2 scoops and its fine, just thicker obviously.
The only plant one I'd rate better that I've tried is Musclenation vanilla, smooth as - but its expensive even when half price, I still have only bought it the once to try.
[Wip3out] Yeah the vanilla is pretty good, better than the choc imo. I've tried basically all plant proteins and I'd rate this as one of the best, but taste is subjective. I might try the berry one this time round.
[Drakesy] Almost out of my berry one so this came just in time
[zfind] Just be wary this and other pea proteins are high in salt, as pointed out by a fellow Ozbargainer.
This particular product is 1060mg/100g.
[SamVicious] Anyone wanting to buy 2 tubs, I recommend checking Commonwealth yello to see if there's a Special.gift gift card offer. I managed to get a $100 gift card for essentially $90 and managed to get 2 tubs with $10.02 remaining which I can use for other stuff.
[levqchi] The chocolate is so bad I had to throw away more than half the tub. Basically not enough chocolate plus the weird aftertaste of artificial sweetener. I find the Coles 100% pea protein plus soymilk more palatable than the chocolate of this
